selected_evidence.requirement: Local caching DNS resolver for system applications
selected_evidence.summary: Unbound configuration validates, the service is enabled and listening on loopback, NetworkManager directs applications to 127.0.0.1, and two identical queries produced one miss and one cache hit.
External resolution worked before and after configuration, through the local cache, through the retained upstream while Unbound was briefly stopped, and again after reboot.

Healthy pre-restart boot ID be303eb3-eeb6-4466-86f1-fd6406dd7dad was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, the new boot ID 28f685c9-6ba6-45fa-8699-5bf877cdeba4 was observed, and post-restart proof confirms the service, listener, configuration, resolver order, external lookup, and cache behavior recovered.

set -eu
config_tmp=$(mktemp /etc/unbound/conf.d/.local-cache.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -f "$config_tmp"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
cat > "$config_tmp" <<'ANTRIEB_UNBOUND_EOF'
# Local caching resolver for system applications.
server:
    interface: 127.0.0.1
    interface: ::1
    access-control: 127.0.0.0/8 allow
    access-control: ::1/128 allow
    hide-identity: yes
    hide-version: yes

forward-zone:
    name: "."
    forward-addr: 10.100.109.1
ANTRIEB_UNBOUND_EOF
chmod 0644 "$config_tmp"
mv "$config_tmp" /etc/unbound/conf.d/local-cache.conf
trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM
restorecon /etc/unbound/conf.d/local-cache.conf
unbound-checkconf
printf '\ninstalled configuration:\n'
cat /etc/unbound/conf.d/local-cache.conf
